title: Downhole Seismic — Interval Velocity

Vs.description: Interval shear wave velocity between two measurement depths

t₁, t₂.description: S-wave travel times to each depth

applicability: For offset source, correct ray path: Vs = √[(z₂-z₁)² + x²] - √[(z₁-z₁)² + x²]) ... use slant-path correction. Typically compute Vs in 1–2 m intervals. First-arrival picking is critical — use reversed-polarity S-wave source for clear identification.

title: Crosshole Seismic — Direct Velocity

V.description: P-wave or S-wave velocity between boreholes

d.description: True distance between source and receiver (from deviation surveys)

applicability: Requires deviation survey of all boreholes (inclinometer). True distance at each depth may differ from surface separation. Three-borehole setup allows straight-ray velocity calculation without assumptions about borehole positions.

title: Dynamic Elastic Moduli from Vp and Vs
alt_forms: G_dyn = ρ × Vs²;  ν_dyn = (Vp² - 2Vs²) / (2(Vp² - Vs²));  K_dyn = ρ × (Vp² - 4Vs²/3)
applicability: Dynamic moduli are measured at very small strains (~10⁻⁶) and are higher than static moduli. Ratio E_static/E_dynamic typically 0.3–0.8 for rock. Poisson's ratio: ν < 0.5; if Vp/Vs → ∞ (saturated soft soil), ν → 0.5.
source: Mavko et al. (2009) Rock Physics Handbook

title: Fracture Dip from Televiewer Sinusoid

A.description: Peak-to-trough amplitude of sinusoid on unwrapped image

applicability: On unwrapped 360° image, a planar feature intersecting a circular borehole appears as a sinusoid. The azimuth of the lowest point of the sinusoid = dip direction (for vertical borehole). For inclined boreholes, correct for borehole orientation to get true dip/dip direction.

title: Archie's Law — Formation Resistivity
applicability: For clean (non-clay) formations. Clay adds surface conduction that Archie's law does not account for — use Waxman-Smits or dual-water models for shaly formations. Primary petrophysical equation linking resistivity to porosity and saturation.

title: Natural Gamma — Clay Content Estimation (Gamma Ray Index)

I_GR.description: Gamma ray index (0 = clean sand, 1 = pure clay/shale)

GR.description: Measured gamma ray value at depth

applicability: Linear clay volume estimate: V_clay ≈ I_GR. Non-linear corrections (Larionov, Clavier) exist. Potassium feldspar and micas can give false high gamma without clay. Spectral gamma (K, U, Th) helps distinguish clay from non-clay gamma sources.

title: Vp/Vs Ratio — Lithology and Saturation Indicator

Vp/Vs.description: Ratio of P-wave to S-wave velocity

applicability: Typical values: Saturated soft clay: 5–15+ (ν → 0.48–0.50). Saturated sand: 2.0–4.0. Dry sand: 1.5–1.8. Rock: 1.5–2.0. Limestone: 1.8–2.0. Water: Vp/Vs → ∞ (no shear). High Vp/Vs indicates saturation or soft clay; low values indicate dry or stiff material.

title: Stoneley Wave Permeability Indicator
applicability: Stoneley (tube) waves in full-waveform sonic logs are attenuated at permeable zones and open fractures. Qualitative indicator — increased Stoneley attenuation correlates with higher permeability and open fractures. Quantitative permeability estimation requires careful modeling.
